'''''Allium chamaemoly''''', called '''dwarf garlic''', is a species of [[garlic]] native to the [[Mediterranean region]] and cultivated elsewhere for its pretty flowers and potently aromatic bulbs. It is found in the wild in [[Spain]] (incl [[Balearic Islands]]), [[France]] (incl [[Corsica]]), [[Malta]], [[Italy]] (inc [[Sardinia]] and [[Sicily]]), [[Greece]], the [[Balkans]],  [[Algeria]], and [[Morocco]].<ref name=-monica>[https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=295272 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>Bailey, L.H. & E.Z. Bailey. 1976. Hortus Third i–xiv, 1–1290. MacMillan, New York.</ref><ref>[https://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=allium+chamaemoly Altervisea, Schede di Botanica, ''Allium chamaemoly'']</ref><ref>Maire, René Charles Joseph Ernest & Weiller, Marc. 1958. Flore d'Afrique du Nord 5: 286.</ref><ref>[http://www.maltawildplants.com/AMRY/Allium_chamaemoly.php Wild Plants of Malta, dwarf garlic]</ref>

''Allium chamaemoly'' is a small plant growing from an underground bulb. [[Scape (botany)|Scape]] is very short or completely absent, so that the umbel forms at ground level. [[Tepal]]s are white, usually with a purple midvein. Leaves are flat and grass-like, often with long white hairs.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358320#page/313/mode/1up Linnaeus, Carl von. 1753. Species Plantarum 1: 301].</ref>

Two formal botanical varieties are recognized:<ref name=-monica/>
* ''Allium chamaemoly'' subsp. ''chamaemoly'' - most of European species range but not [[North Africa]]
* ''Allium chamaemoly'' subsp. ''longicaulis'' <small>Pastor & Valdés</small> - [[Spain]] (incl [[Balearic Islands|Balearic Is]]), [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]]
